title: Baybay Tall Coconut (BAYT): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Baybay Tall Coconut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Baybay Tall coconut is a coconut variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Baybay Tall is a registered coconut variety, also sold or known as BAYT. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1996 as NSIC 1996 Co 08. Its record notes 2.55 tonnes of copra per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for BAYT, this is the same coconut. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [coconut variety finder](/crop-varieties/coconut), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. blocks.text: Key facts about Baybay Tall coconut
When does it bear, and how much?

Its average yield of 2.55 t copra/ha beats the average of its group, 1.85. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [coconut bud rot](/diseases/coconut-bud-rot).

The pests and diseases that hit coconut fields most often: [coconut bud rot](/diseases/coconut-bud-rot), [coconut cadang cadang](/diseases/cadang-cadang), [coconut leaf beetle (Brontispa)](/pests/coconut-leaf-beetle), [coconut rhinoceros beetle](/pests/coconut-rhinoceros-beetle), [coconut scale insect (cocolisap)](/pests/cocolisap). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its fruiting season is 12, bearing regular. Each palm gave about 108.1 nuts a year in the records, with 294.8 grams of copra per nut.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** About 108 nuts per palm a year, 4.4 t copra/ha.
Resistant to bud rot and foliar decay.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: top copra producer among the registered coconuts (about 4.4 t/ha) and father palm of PCA 15 3. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Baybay Tall coconut

Talls live long and stand typhoons, dwarfs bear early and are easy to harvest, and hybrids between the two give the most copra. Pick by use: copra, buko, or both. Get seednuts from a PCA accredited source. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is BAYT the same as Baybay Tall?
items.a: Yes. BAYT is another name for Baybay Tall, registered as NSIC 1996 Co 08. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows 2.55 tonnes of copra per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Baybay Tall?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
